headline: Shuttle and Permit Requirements for Lake O'Hara and Takkakaw
reservation: Accessing Lake O'Hara requires a highly competitive shuttle reservation through a seasonal lottery or specific booking window. While general park entry is covered by a Discovery Pass, camping and the Burgess Shale guided hikes must be reserved months in advance. Always confirm the current seasonal shuttle schedule via the official Parks Canada portal.

days.title: Glacial Power and Steep Descents
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from the Village of Field

stops.name: Takakkaw Falls
stops.detail: Experience the sheer scale of one of Canada’s highest waterfalls, fed by the Daly Glacier.

stops.name: Meeting of the Waters
stops.detail: Observe the distinct color contrast where the glacial Yoho River joins the clear Kicking Horse River.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for the Yoho Valley Road, including tight switchbacks; conditions vary.
days.note: Yoho Valley Road is seasonal and typically closed to all vehicles from October to June.

days.title: Ancient Seas and Emerald Waters
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Emerald Lake Lodge

stops.name: Emerald Lake
stops.detail: Walk the lakeshore trail to see the vivid green water caused by powdered limestone called rock flour.

stops.name: Natural Bridge
stops.detail: View the powerful Kicking Horse River as it carves through solid ancient rock layers.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes from Field to Emerald Lake; parking is extremely limited midday.
days.note: Canoe rentals are popular here; arrive before 10 AM to minimize wait times during peak July and August weeks.

days.title: The Kicking Horse Pass and Spiral Tunnels
days.start: Suggested: 9:30 AM from Spiral Tunnels Viewpoint

stops.name: Upper Spiral Tunnel Viewpoint
stops.detail: Watch for freight trains navigating the ingenious engineering of the mountain rail system.

stops.name: Wapta Falls
stops.detail: Take the forested trail to the largest waterfall on the Kicking Horse River by volume.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for the distance between the tunnels and the western Wapta Falls trailhead.
days.note: Wapta Falls involves a moderate walk; ensure you have time for the return trip before park light fades.

intel.title: Emerald Lake Overflow
intel.text: The main lot at Emerald Lake frequently reaches capacity by 10 AM. Parks Canada may implement traffic control on the access road during holiday weekends.

intel.title: Mountain Topography Effects
intel.text: Reliable signal is found in the town of Field along the Trans-Canada Highway. Most of the Yoho Valley and Emerald Lake backcountry remain in a communication dead zone.

intel.title: Gateway Gas Stations
intel.text: The village of Field has limited fuel; larger service centers are located in Golden or Banff. Ensure your tank is sufficient for the return climb over the Kicking Horse Pass.

intel.title: Switchback Limits
intel.text: The Yoho Valley Road features steep, narrow switchbacks requiring a specific 3-point turn for most vehicles. Plan for slower travel times than standard highway distances suggest.

intel.title: Lake O'Hara Restrictions
intel.text: Private vehicles are prohibited on the 11km Lake O'Hara access road. Access is strictly limited to those with shuttle reservations, valid camping permits, or those walking the distance.

plan.arrival: Depart Calgary (YYC) and travel west through Banff. The village of Field is the central hub for local guest houses and basic supplies before exploring the high-valley trailheads.
plan.vehicle: Suitable for most cars, but trailers and RVs over a certain length are discouraged on the Yoho Valley Road switchbacks.
plan.goldenHour: Finn Creek or the Natural Bridge provide exceptional late-afternoon vistas as the sun dips below the President Range.
